 Unions
Minimum wage
Corporate power
Child labor
The case for tripling union membership
How rebuilding union power would strengthen workers, the economy, and our democracy

First-of-its-kind analysis measures how expanding union membership would boost wages, lower inequality, and benefit communities and democracy. The report estimates that tripling union membership would:  

  • Deliver a 14.5% raise for the median worker—amounting to more than $7,700 annually, or nearly $270,000 over a 35-year career.
  • Shift $1.2 trillion to workers annually. 
  • Raise wages in every state.   
  • Significantly narrow racial wage gaps. 

Read now →

Related

  • 50 million workers want to join a union: What if they did? 
  • Workers’ resolve drives increase in unionization in 2025
  • U.S. employers spend more than $1.5 billion annually on union avoidance
  • Americans favor unions over big business now more than ever
  • Sectoral bargaining FAQ
  • Holding the line: Rights to unionize and collectively bargain
Seventeen states and localities are increasing their minimum wage this July

On July 1, the minimum wage will increase in Alaska, Oregon, and Washington, D.C.—lifting wages for more than 361,000 workers and collectively raising their earnings by more than $221 million.

In addition to these two states and D.C., 14 cities and counties are also increasing their minimum wage this summer, including Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.

Learn more about where the minimum wage is going up and how that has positive impacts on more than the people who earn it →

Related

  • Myths vs. facts about the minimum wage
  • Trump’s war in Iran has wiped out 1.5 years of wage growth
  • Setting high standards for a federal minimum wage
  • Minimum wage tracker
  • A history of the minimum wage: 85 years later, the minimum wage is far from equitable
U.S. employers spend more than $1.5 billion annually on union avoidance

NEW: U.S. employers spend roughly $1.7 billion a year on union avoidance consultants and law firms to keep their workers from organizing and bargaining for better pay and working conditions, according to our new report with LaborLab. 

While research shows many nonunion workers want to join a union, U.S. labor law allows employers to derail workers’ unionization efforts with impunity. 

It doesn’t have to be this way →

Related

  • Unlawful: U.S. employers are charged with violating federal law in 41.5% of all union election campaigns
  • Why workers need the Protecting the Right to Organize Act
  • Unions aren’t just good for workers—they also benefit communities and democracy
Efforts to strengthen child labor protections have stalled

Despite rising child labor violations, at least 13 state legislatures have attempted to roll back child labor standards this year. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has undermined federal enforcement of child labor standards. 

While a few states are strengthening protections, more state lawmakers should take action to combat this growing child labor crisis. 

It doesn’t have to be this way →

Related

  • New research reveals how work permits reduce child labor violations
  • Child labor standards: State solutions to the U.S. worker rights crisis
  • States can do more to hold the line against escalating federal attacks on workers’ rights

Unequal Power

Shattering the myth of equal power in the workplace. Unequal power

We envision an economy that is just and strong, sustainable, and equitable--where every job is good, every worker can join a union, and every family and community can thrive.

EPI is a leader in the movement for economic justice. We use the tools of economics to win policy change that advances power for workers, economic security for families, and racial and gender equity in our nation.

臺灣經濟受惠於AI與半導體產業，動能穩健；但隨著大國的貿易保護政策與碳務制度實施，全球供應鏈將進入高成本競爭時代。面對地緣政治引發的挑戰，本期焦點透過五篇專文，...

經濟前瞻第222期：川普新政三百日：臺灣的挑戰

川普2025年1月重返白宮後，迄今已約三百日，其以「美國優先」為核心的經貿與產業政策，打亂原本的全球供應鏈體系與經濟秩序。臺灣作為全球科技與供應鏈樞紐，正處於調...

經濟前瞻第221期：WTO三十載的效益、挑戰與展望

世界貿易組織自1995年成立迄2025年恰屆滿30周年，成立後推動多邊、複邊貿易談判，實施WTO會員貿易政策審查機制與改善爭端解決程序，對全球貿易自由化、透明化...

經濟前瞻第220期：碳、關稅與科技：運輸業的全球三重壓力

全球運輸業正迎來「碳、關稅、科技」三股壓力交織而成的轉型挑戰，本期前瞻焦點即從這三個面向切入，解析產業所面對的衝擊與應對策略。首先聚焦碳議題，探討國內碳盤查法規...

經濟前瞻第219期：新關稅時代下的永續啟航：全球政經震盪中的臺灣永續契機

川普重返白宮後，激起全球關稅政策新一波震盪，臺灣不僅要應對來自美中貿易與關稅戰的壓力，也需積極布局未來永續發展之路。本期《經濟前瞻》以「第五屆臺灣循環經濟獎」的...

經濟前瞻第218期：中國製造2025

本期前瞻焦點以中國議題為核心，2025年適逢《中國製造2025》實施10週年，這項十年前啟動的製造業升級計畫，曾被視為中國邁向製造強國的關鍵一步，如今成效如何？...

2025年全球經濟展望專書──全球局勢風雲起 經濟安全優先

中華經濟研究院身為國內重要經濟智庫，向來致力提供優質資訊分析此項任務，每年年初更主動提出全球、中國大陸及臺灣經濟資訊供社會大眾參考。《2025年全球經濟展望》專...

經濟前瞻第217期：川普再度執政：臺灣在新經濟環境中的挑戰與機會

2025年對全球影響最大的事件，就是川普再度成為美國總統，國際政治經濟局勢恐因此將進入一個混亂脫序的時代。然而從川普的不可預測性中，本期經濟前瞻嘗試針對蓬勃發展...

經濟前瞻第216期：全球高漲的經濟安全意識

近來隨著美中經貿對抗、地緣政治衝突升高，全球經濟安全意識日益高漲。面對國際局勢的轉變，處於地緣政治衝突節點上的臺灣，更應掌握最新動態，瞭解主要國家如何維護經濟安...

CELEBRATING 80 YEARS OF LIBERTY

In 1946, Leonard E. Read established the Foundation for Economic Education (FEE) as the original free market education organization in the U.S.

Eighty years later, the mission remains the same: to inspire, educate, and connect future leaders with the economic, ethical, and legal principles of a free society.

Timeless principles never go out of style.

Learn the Ideas of Freedom.
Change the World.

Founded in 1946, FEE is the original home of free-market economic thinking in America.

FEE’s popular digital content and in-person programs turn complex ideas into practical tools for living your best life and making the world a better place.

Welcome to C2ES

Our mission is to secure a safe and stable climate by accelerating the global transition to net-zero greenhouse gas emissions and a thriving, just, and resilient economy.

About C2ES

The Latest from C2ES

Support Our Work

Donate

Accelerating the US Net-Zero Transition

C2ES works to build broad, durable support for effective and ambitious climate policies, built on partnerships and equity, and anchored in deep understanding among communities, businesses, and policymakers throughout the country of the tangible economic opportunities that the net-zero transition will create.

THE NET-ZERO TRANSITION

Supporting the Paris Agreement

C2ES has been deeply involved in the United Nations climate talks for many years, producing expert analysis on issues facing negotiators, and facilitating informal dialogue among key countries.

SUPPORTING THE PARIS AGREEMENT

Building Climate Resilience

In the face of increasing climate impacts, climate resilience is critical for communities and businesses to thrive. C2ES advances new resilience strategies, provides leading policy analysis, and convenes stakeholders around emerging challenges to build broad support for action and make investment in resilience a clear choice for public and private decision-makers.
